title: Opuscula cum Vita
shelf_note: Pico's 1498 collected works (Vita by Gianfrancesco, Apologia, Oration, etc.); the Apologia and Oration defend magic and Kabbalah, so it belongs on a Latin-Kabbalah shelf.
structure_note: Counts are clean (303 records, all OCR'd and translated, no duplicates). But the page text is not: of four sampled pages, one OCR field holds model reasoning instead of a transcription (p.106), one holds a string of combining macrons (p.237), and one stops after 11 lines (p.165). The translations of those pages were not made from the page.
reader_summary: This is Pico della Mirandola's 1498 Opera (Opuscula) with Gianfrancesco Pico's Life. The Life page is well transcribed and faithfully translated, but in the Apologia and the Oration the transcription is broken or missing, and the English shown there is either a free summary or a passage from elsewhere in the Oration. A reader cannot trust that the English on any page matches the page.

title: Doctissimi Viri Ioannis Pici Mirandulae, Concordiae comitis: Exactissima expositio in orationem dominicam
shelf_note: Pico's exposition of the Lord's Prayer (1537 print) is devotional; nothing kabbalistic on the sampled pages. It is on the shelf by author only.
structure_note: 34 leaves, all OCR'd and translated, no duplicates. Page 29 was OCR'd by a different engine (flash-lite, pipeline_preview) with a bracketed-expansion convention unlike the other pages.
reader_summary: A short devotional commentary by Pico on the Lord's Prayer, in a small 1537 octavo. The transcription is of the right text and the English is a close, reliable translation on three of four pages; the fourth (p.29) has misexpanded abbreviations and an English last sentence that runs past the page. It is a Pico text, not a kabbalistic one.

ocr_errors.problem: bleed-through side-note recorded as this page's margin

other.note: scan note 'Minor ink bleed-through from the preceding page is visible on the left margin.' rendered as a <note> in the English pane

tr_errors.english: we shall see that which was fulfilled for the virgin: He has filled the hungry
tr_errors.problem: should be 'that saying of the Virgin fulfilled' (the Magnificat); the Virgin is the speaker, not the beneficiary

ocr_errors.problem: 'eo' wrongly expanded to 'eorum'; long s read as f
abbreviation misexpanded into a new verb 'mundat'

tr_errors.source: More ei⁹ q sit ifirm⁹: q vbi sana (page ends)
tr_errors.english: Like the custom of one who is ill: who, when he has been healed, asks the doctor to give him some medicine or a way of life, so that he may preserve his health.
tr_errors.problem: English completes the sentence with content from the next page (or invents it)

book_verdict: Clean small book with good transcriptions and translations on most pages; one lite-OCR page has misexpanded abbreviations and a run-on English ending. Sound, but it is Pico's devotional writing, not Kabbalah.

title: Artis cabalisticae. Tomus I
shelf_note: Pistorius's 1587 anthology of Christian Kabbalah (Ricius, Leone Ebreo, Reuchlin): the core of the shelf.
structure_note: 1,136 page records against pages_count 1,120 and pages_translated 1,114 (field drift of 16). Printed numbers run 113, 381, 676, 962 at records 183, 492, 813, 1116, a slowly growing offset consistent with one continuous pagination plus unnumbered leaves. 72 backsteps / 116 repeats on 1,072 printed numbers is more than misread numerals alone would give; worth a structure check, but the sampled leaves are all right and in order.
reader_summary: Volume I of Pistorius's Artis cabalisticae (Basel 1587), the standard Renaissance collection of Christian-Kabbalah texts: on these pages Ricius's De coelesti agricultura IV, Leone Ebreo's Dialogue II, and Reuchlin's De arte cabalistica and De verbo mirifico. The transcriptions are of the right leaves and nearly complete, and the English is close and careful. Watch for an occasional dropped sentence and headings the translator supplied.

tr_errors.english: The previous page concluded the correspondence of Emperor Constantine regarding the Arian controversy.
tr_errors.problem: continuity claim not on the page and unlikely for this volume

tr_errors.problem: heading supplied by the translator, not on the page

tr_errors.source: difficile nobis, ex ineffabili uocem flecti, qua obedienter utamur
tr_errors.english: it is difficult for us to be moved by a voice from the ineffable

book_verdict: The strongest book in the packet: right leaves, near-complete transcriptions, faithful English on the core Christian-Kabbalah texts. Minor slips only; the page-count drift deserves a structure audit.

title: [Vocabularius breviloquus]
shelf_note: A 1478 Latin school dictionary (Vocabularius breviloquus, attributed to Reuchlin). It is a lexicon of ordinary Latin, not a work of Kabbalah; it is on the shelf by Reuchlin's name only.
structure_note: Text and image are one leaf apart on all four sampled pages: each image shows the leaf after the one transcribed (p.103 image Carduus-Caro, text Carabrio-Cardularij; p.323 image Nitrum-Nomen, text Nicola-Nitrum; p.381 image Precentor-Prefatus, text Pragmatica-Prebenda; p.583 image Mechor-Mereo, text Madidus-Maturo). This looks like a book-wide offset. 13 pages are untranslated.
reader_summary: This is the incunable Latin dictionary Vocabularius breviloquus, not a kabbalistic work. On every sampled page the transcription is of the previous leaf, so the image and text never match, and the transcription itself garbles headwords (Carto for Carbo, Nilns, Numbus). The English inherits those errors and adds glosses that are not in the source.
